newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary shares end mixed, BUX continues to ease.
newsitem.headline: Hungary shares end mixed, BUX continues to ease.

text.p: Hungarian shares, led by oil and gas company MOL, rebounded from Wednesday's sharp falls, traders said.
Sixteen of the 35 shares traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange rose and 14 stocks eased, with the BUX index closing down by 35.46 points at 5,333.18.
Traders said the market sentiment was still mixed but reflected improvement since Wednesday when profit-taking trimmed prices.

"If we look at the main papers, the trend for today was rising compared with yesterday's closing prices," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities, adding that the BUX index is calculated by average prices and sometimes did not accurately reflect trends based on closing prices.
Traders said profit-taking was likely to continue, but the market's direction would be determined by the 1996 results of the most liquid shares.
The market is especially looking forward to the results of MOL, the chemicals and drugs producers.
"If these results are good, and good results are expected, then the (declining) trend will reverse," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft.
MOL, which was among the top losers on Wednesday, rebounded and finished at 3,400 forints, up 220.
Traders views were mixed over Inter-Europa Bank results. They regarded plastics company Pannonplast figures as good.
After the release of the preliminary figures, Inter-Europa closed at 49,000 forints, down 1,500, while Pannonplast firmed 150 forints to finish at 7,100.
Hungarian bourse-listed companies have to release preliminary 1996 results by February 15.
